item.title: Chiral or unidirectional? Multiterminal current partition in the quantum Hall regime from self-consistent screening theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.17441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiterminal current measurements on a six-terminal Hall bar were recently used to argue that the current flow is chiral on the quantized Hall plateaus and non-chiral between them, and, in a companion analysis, that the imposed current flows along one edge only. We examine these conclusions with the self-consistent screening theory of the quantum Hall effect. The plateau values of the current partition follow from a vanishing longitudinal conductivity and a quantized Hall conductivity alone: every two-dimensional conductor with $\sigma_\ell=0$ and $\sigma_{\rm H}=\nu e^2/h$ has the conductance matrix of the "coherent and chiral" model, whatever the spatial distribution of the current. Terminal currents fix the current density only up to circulating currents, made explicit here with a stream function, and the chirality of the current density is a property of exactly this part. A two-dimensional local transport calculation for the measured device, including its two interior contacts, reproduces the plateau partition for all contact configurations and the ordering of the suppression between the plateaus without edge channels. The self-consistent current density separates into a chiral equilibrium (magnetization) current, which carries no net current, and a transport current that flows in the same direction in both edge strips; the "one-edge" imposed current is a bookkeeping choice of the reference chemical potential. The floating potentials of the two interior contacts are predicted to be equal when the bulk around them is quantized and to differ by up to half the Hall voltage when the current flows in edge strips. Multiterminal current partition measures the sign of the Hall conductivity and the absence of dissipation, not the location or the chirality of the transport current; the edge channels are the premise of the interpretation, not a result of the measurement.
item.dc:creator: Afif Siddiki

item.title: Roton softening and crystallization in a mass-asymmetric electron-hole bilayer
item.description: arXiv:2611.17474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether roton softening drives a continuous transition into a density-ordered or supersolid state is a longstanding question in interacting quantum fluids. Here, we address this microscopically in a mass-asymmetric electron--hole bilayer in which exciton condensation competes with interaction-driven crystallization. Using self-consistent Hartree--Fock--Bogoliubov theory and its time-dependent extension, we show that increasing the carrier-mass ratio or interlayer distance induces a pronounced roton minimum in the homogeneous exciton condensate liquid. The system undergoes a first-order transition to a crystalline state, preempting the roton instability. In this metastable regime, strongly interacting holes first drive the crystallization of the itinerant electrons, and the system then evolves into a hole-crystal--electron-metal phase at larger interlayer distance. Supersolid solutions with coexisting interlayer coherence and charge density order are also found to be energetically competitive near the crystallization boundary. We further discuss our findings based on recent experimental setups in two-dimensional material heterostructures.
item.dc:creator: Ambuj Jain, Mu-Yang Chen, Chao-Xing Liu, Binghai Yan, Wangqian Miao

item.title: Non-ergodic Area Scaling of Andreev Transport in Al/AlO$_x$/Al Tunnel Junctions
item.description: arXiv:2611.17511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: State-of-the-art superconducting qubits rely on Al/AlO$_x$/Al Josephson junctions (JJs) as a nonlinear element with an ideal sinusoidal current-phase dependence, with its inductance set by the junction area and oxidation conditions. This idealization holds only if the many conduction channels through the amorphous AlO$_x$ barrier transmit weakly and almost identically. Here, we measure the second-order subgap Andreev current, which sets the second Josephson harmonic, in Al/AlO$_x$/Al JJs. For junction sizes relevant to qubits, we find that this current is dominated by $\lesssim 300$ effective channels whose transparencies exceed the ideal tunneling limit ($\lesssim 10^{-6}$) by orders of magnitude. For small and high-aspect-ratio junctions, increasing the junction size does not average out the effect of these high transparency channels but instead adds additional channels of even greater transparency. The trend inverts once both the width and length of the junction exceed a critical length scale, above which the effective transparency decreases with area. This non-ergodic scaling of the Andreev current is reproduced by simulations and attributed to non-self-averaging statistics of the transparency distribution, which arise from variations in oxide thickness. The effect is largely invisible to the normal-state conductance used to target the inductance and reveals unexpected geometric and size-related trade-offs for scaling superconducting qubit systems to large numbers of junctions.
item.dc:creator: David J. Perello, Marco Coraiola, Minje Park, Cliff Chen, Hanho Lee, Abhishek Banerjee, Gil Refael, Yuki Sato

item.title: Thermally Activated Magnetic Switching in Antiferromagnetic Van der Waals Trilayers Resolved by Single-Spin Diamond Magnetometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.17521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Van der Waals magnets provide a versatile platform for exploring magnetic phenomena that emerge from reduced dimensionality, including layer-dependent magnetic ordering. Here, we use scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond magnetometry to measure the magnetization of a trilayer of the A-type antiferromagnet CrPS$_4$, resolving its zero-field bistability between the up-down-up ($\uparrow\downarrow\uparrow$) and down-up-down ($\downarrow\uparrow\downarrow$) layer magnetization configurations. The coercive field decreases approximately linearly with temperature, consistent with the N\'eel--Arrhenius model. Density Functional Theory calculations capture the temperature dependence of the magnetization and determine the coercive field in the coherent-rotation case. The measured coercive fields are lower, identifying thermally activated domain nucleation as the reversal mechanism. Spatial magnetic imaging supports this picture, revealing independently switching regions likely pinned by structural inhomogeneities. Our results highlight the power of scanning NV magnetometry for the quantitative investigation of magnetization reversal in two-dimensional magnets, unraveling the magnetic phenomenology that emerges in low-dimensional systems.
item.dc:creator: Fabian A. Gerritsma, Roland W. Mulder, Bal\'azs Nagyfalusi, Pieter C. J. A. van Zweeden, Samer Kurdi, Francisco Machado, Jaime Ferrer, Samuel Ma\~nas-Valero, Toeno van der Sar

item.title: Chiral topological phases of proximitized planar germanium
item.description: arXiv:2611.17579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the topological phase diagram of a two-dimensional hole gas in planar germanium resulting from the combination of spin-orbit coupling, proximity-induced $s$-wave superconductivity, and magnetization. The peculiarity of the hole gas is the presence of a Rashba spin-orbit interaction cubic in momentum, possibly coexisting with a linear term, which results in the presence of distinct topological phases with Chern numbers as high as four. We map out the topological phase diagram based on effective single-band models with and without spin, and use input parameters based on a self-consistent Schr\"odinger-Poisson calculation of a planar germanium hole gas. As a concrete model for inducing magnetization in the hole gas, we consider the exchange interaction coming from the presence of a dilute ensemble of manganese impurities. A topological phase with $C=3$ could be accessible experimentally in unstrained planar germanium.
item.dc:creator: Vittorio Coppini, Bernard van Heck

item.title: Selective coupling and spectral evolution of topological domain-wall states under local perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we investigate the spectral evolution of topological domain-wall states in a one-dimensional structure described by the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model. We show that a local potential applied to the domain wall induces a selective coupling between a topological state and specific bulk states. Moreover, by increasing the gate potential, we observe that the domain wall state energies asymptotically reach a bulk band, whereas new domain wall states appear on the opposite side of the band. As a consequence, the domain-wall-state spectrum evolves through a sequence of localized states that remain separated from the bulk continuum. These effects are also reflected in transport calculations, where the conductance peaks follow the evolution of the energy spectrum. To experimentally verify these phenomena, we realize an RLC topo-electrical circuit and perform impedance spectroscopy measurements. We find that the impedance matches the local density of states, exhibiting resonances at frequencies associated with the bulk energies that selectively couple to the domain wall topological state.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Y. D\'iaz-Bonifaz, Edna M. Hern\'andez, Carlos Ram\'irez

item.title: A Unified Device-Level Physical Framework for DRAM Read Disturbance
item.description: arXiv:2611.17634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Read disturbance in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) depends on both local device interactions and the electrical conditions imposed by shared array circuitry. Here, we combine DIMM-level characterization results, device measurements, and TCAD simulations to interpret RowHammer, RowPress, and ColumnDisturb within a unified device-level physical framework. We relate charge evolution at the floating storage node to three key mechanisms: trap-assisted electron migration (EM), capacitive coupling (CC), and sense-amplifier-mediated disturb (SAMD). EM is local and trap-sensitive, while CC weakens with wordline separation. SAMD extends disturbance through shared column circuitry by modifying unselected-cell leakage under rail-level bitline biases, a contribution supported by the approximately ninefold higher OFF-state leakage measured relative to retention-like conditions for a high-voltage storage state. These distinct spatial ranges account for localized RowHammer and RowPress failures and remote ColumnDisturb populations with abrupt changes at subarray boundaries. We further interpret prolonged RowPress activation as a transition from an initial RowHammer-like transient to sustained leakage driven mainly by SAMD under held wordline and bitline biases. Within this device-level framework, trap effectiveness and storage-state-dependent leakage provide an interpretation of previously puzzling failure signatures, including the earlier onset of 0-to-1 RowHammer failures despite the predominance of 1-to-0 failures at high hammer counts. The same framework explains the observed RowPress and ColumnDisturb polarities and the duration-dependent reversal of neighboring- and passing-wordline effectiveness. These results provide a physical basis for developing compact DRAM reliability models across access patterns and array configurations.
item.dc:creator: Zhaoqiang Bai, Haocong Luo, Xinhe Wang, Xujing Li, Yuelin Jiang, Xuelu Huang, Guilei Wang, Hao Meng, Ataberk Olgun, Ismail Emir Yuksel, F. Nisa Bostanc{\i}, Jikun Wang, Onur Mutlu

item.title: Quantum spin-wave statistics and dimensionality in thermally activated magnetic transitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.17641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A quantum correction to the rate of thermally activated transition between magnetic states is formulated within harmonic transition state theory and the Kramers-Langer theory by employing quantum statistics for stable spin-wave excitations around the initial state and the transition state. Quantum spin-wave statistics modifies both parameters of the Arrhenius expression for the transition rate relative to their classical values: the zero-point fluctuations renormalize the energy barrier, while the Bose-Einstein occupation of the spin-wave modes modifies the pre-exponential factor. Comparison of the classical and quantum-statistical pre-exponential factors reveals a systematic error associated with the excessive weight assigned to high-frequency excitations by classical equipartition. This error accumulates over the spin-wave spectrum and becomes increasingly severe with increasing dimensionality of the system. The effect is demonstrated for coherent magnetization reversal, and transitions involving noncollinear magnetic textures, including collapse of a magnetic skyrmion and rupture of a skyrmion tube, where classical and quantum-statistical predictions for the transition rate can differ by many orders of magnitude in three-dimensional systems.
item.dc:creator: Jacob J. Mankenberg, Grzegorz J. Kwiatkowski, Pavel F. Bessarab

item.title: Low-Temperature Heat Capacity of Single-Walled Carbon Nanotube Bundles with low dimensional gas systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.18010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-temperature heat-capacity data for pristine single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) bundles and for SWCNT/gas systems containing adsorbed Xe, Ne, N2, and CH4 were analyzed within a phenomenological framework. The data were fitted within the phenomenological form C(T) = C3T3 + C5T5, where the coefficients are interpreted as effective parameters of the coupled SWCNT-adsorbate excitation spectrum. Pristine SWCNT bundles exhibit a negative C5 coefficient, reflecting a non-Debye dispersive contribution associated with low-energy flexural-like modes. Gas adsorption systematically modifies both C3 and C5, indicating that the adsorbate's heat-capacity contribution may not be treated as fully independent. The Xe series suggests that mass loading, modified adsorbate-nanotube interaction, and changes in intertube coupling slightly reshape the nanotube vibrational response. Coverage-dependent measurements for Ne reveal a progressive shift from nanotube-dominated excitations toward domination of additional low-energy adsorbate modes in the phonon spectrum of the SWCNT-Ne system, while molecular adsorbates (N2, CH4) introduce translational, librational, orientational, and rotational degrees of freedom that generate correspondingly stronger perturbations.
item.dc:creator: M. S. Barabashko, A. I. Krivchikov

item.title: Tunable Valley Filtering and Splitting via Gate Control in Wrinkled Graphene
item.description: arXiv:2611.18042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the use of strain-induced wrinkles in graphene nanoribbons to achieve tunable valley filtering and splitting, crucial for advancing valleytronic devices. By combining tight-binding simulations, strain tensor analysis, and quantum transport calculations, we explicitly demonstrate that wrinkle-induced pseudomagnetic fields facilitate current splitting and valley-selective filtering in folded graphene nanoribbons based on wrinkle parameters like height, strain spreading/deformation and wrinkle orientation (tilt angle). Moreover, we show that the application of a top-gate voltage provides dynamic control over valley splitting, allowing a continuous transition from well-separated valley currents to valley merging as the gate voltage increases. In other parameter regimes, valley filtering arises from an initial current-splitting mechanism, exhibiting a clear gate-controlled transition between distinct transport behaviors. Our results offer new insights into strain-engineered valley transport and suggest a promising pathway toward practical graphene-based valleytronic devices.
item.dc:creator: C. I. Osuala, A. Belayadi, M. Moutan, S. Elatresh, A. Johanson, A. Abbout

item.title: Charge-tunable acoustic surface plasmons in topological nodal-line semimetals
item.description: arXiv:2611.18158v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological nodal-line semimetals host drumhead surface states, carrying a large surface density of states. We show that these states support an acoustic surface plasmon, whose velocity is strongly enhanced by the Coulomb interaction. At sufficiently small wavevectors, the mode lies above the surface particle-hole continuum and below both mixed surface-bulk absorption thresholds, leaving bulk particle-hole creation as the leading damping channel. Near drumhead depletion, the dispersion is highly sensitive to the surface charge, which suggests applications of plasmon spectroscopy of nodal-line semimetals to sensing technologies.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Buccheri, Francesco M. D. Pellegrino, Jeroen van den Brink

item.title: Digitally-alloyed magnetic topological insulator nanostructures grown via stencil mask molecular beam epitaxy
item.description: arXiv:2611.18280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic topological insulator nanostructures are a promising platform for the realization of fault-tolerant quantum computation. For this, such nanostructures need to be embedded into the necessary superconducting architectures. In this study, we demonstrate a method for the growth of magnetic topological insulator nanostructures via molecular beam epitaxy, utilising digital alloying and defining their shapes in-situ by stencil mask technology. Cr-doped (Bi$_y$Sb$_{1-y}$)$_2$Te$_3$ micro- and nanometer-sized Hall bars are fabricated and the magneto-transport properties for various Cr doping amounts and different Hall bar dimensions are investigated at low temperatures. We find indications that the Fermi energy is located inside the bulk band gap, while disorder and charge puddles affect the transport behaviour. Furthermore, we investigate the magnetic properties and discuss the transition from ferromagnetic to paramagnetic behaviour.
item.dc:creator: Jan Karthein, Max Va{\ss}en-Carl, Lars Maier, Abdur Rehman Jalil, Gion Toehgiono, Josua Thieme, Julian Feldewerth, Benjamin Bennemann, Joscha Domnick, Taizo Kawano, Sosuke Otsubo, Ren\'e Heller, Jun Ishihara, Detlev Gr\"utzmacher, Makoto Kohda, Peter Sch\"uffelgen, Thomas Sch\"apers

item.title: Quantized resistance limitations for graphene p-n junction devices
item.description: arXiv:2611.18318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Developing high-resistance quantized Hall resistance standards requires accessing values beyond the robust value seen in epitaxial graphene (R_{\mathrm{H}}=\ \frac{1}{2}\frac{h}{e^{2}}). This study evaluates the available parameter space of the coefficient of effective resistance across various epitaxial graphene p-n junction topologies, including rectangular, Corbino, and triangular layouts. Because mapping desired resistances to device configurations is mathematically degenerate, an automated Landauer-B\"uttiker Python solver was developed for all three topologies and was validated by cryogenic multi-terminal transport measurements and LTspice simulations. By analyzing the Shannon entropy of available states, it is found that rectangular checkerboards maximize topological complexity and tunable outputs, whereas Corbino geometries exhibit highly constrained resistance availabilities.
item.dc:creator: Tamar M. Padwa, DaVonne Henry, Dominick S. Scaletta, Heather M. Hill, Antonio L. Levy, Dean G. Jarrett, David B. Newell, Albert F. Rigosi

item.title: Symmetry induced spin splitting of topological surface states at equal carrier density
item.description: arXiv:2611.18342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface states are among the most striking consequences of band inversion in topological materials. In magnetotransport of three-dimensional topological insulators, the typical signature of surface state transport is a quantized Hall conductance with nontrivial sequences of integer filling factors, varying with the total carrier density. For two independent Dirac carriers, one expects Hall plateaus only at odd-integer filling factors. In this work, we report the observation of symmetry induced spin splitting in magnetotransport experiments on a dual-gate three-dimensional topological insulator device based on HgTe. In the topological surface state regime, we observe Hall plateaus at both odd and even integers when we gate the device symmetrically, i.e., with equal density at the top and bottom. This phenomenon originates in structural inversion symmetry, which remarkably induces a spin splitting and forces the eigenstates to be symmetric and antisymmetric linear combinations of the top and bottom surface states. This is in contrast with two-dimensional systems, where spin splitting is caused by absence of inversion symmetry. We interpret the experimental observations with a perturbative model using isoparity eigenstates, the conserved quantum number associated with structural inversion. The result demonstrates that the picture where the top and bottom states are treated as independent Dirac carriers is not valid when the carrier density is symmetric.
item.dc:creator: Wouter Beugeling, Shyam Sundar Yadav, Maximilian Hofer, Valentin L. M\"uller, Moritz Siebert, Tobias Kie{\ss}ling, Ewelina M. Hankiewicz, Hartmut Buhmann, Laurens W. Molenkamp

item.title: Topological Hybridization Gaps from Molecular Orbitals Coupled to Dirac Fermions
item.description: arXiv:2611.18400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A magnetically gapped topological-insulator surface carries a half-quantized Hall response. We show that hybridizing the surface Dirac fermions with a flat band of chiral orbitals adds an integer to it: spin-momentum locking forces the hybridization to wind around the band-crossing ring, opening a topological gap. For orbitals with total angular momentum $j$, rotational symmetry fixes the surface Hall conductivity to $je^2/h$, with the sign set by the Dirac branch crossed and independent of the sign of the Dirac mass. The result survives crystal-field quenching of the orbital moment, with the winding then set by interference between hybridization pathways. First-principles calculations for a monolayer of nitric oxide adsorbed on Bi$_2$Se$_3$ predict a $\sim 20$ meV hybridization gap and an intrinsic surface Hall conductivity of $\frac{3}{2}e^2/h$, identifying molecular orbital angular momentum as a handle on surface topology.
item.dc:creator: Juli\'an Castro, Jorge I. Facio, Ver\'onica Vildosola

item.title: Topological phase diagram of an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with negative coupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.18456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with three atoms per unit cell has been experimentally realized in perovskite exciton-polariton micropillars. A distinctive feature of this system is that the second and third bands undergo a topological transition through a band crossing at the wave vector $k=0$, associated with a negative coupling. In this work, we analytically determine the phase diagram of the model as a function of the on-site energy splitting and the ratio of intercell to intracell hopping amplitudes. We identify seven regions in this lane, with four distinct topological phases, characterized by different Zak phases of the three bands. Our results provide a useful theoretical framework for interpreting existing experiments and serve as a guide for future experimental investigations of this system.
item.dc:creator: P. A. Grizzi, P. Roura-Bas, A. A. Aligia

item.title: Quantum melting and Pomeranchuk effect of zero-field Wigner solids
item.description: arXiv:2611.18532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wigner solids and crystals are many-body phases of matter in which repulsive interactions between the charge carriers cause them to freeze into a solid. How Wigner solids compete or cooperate with integer and fractional quantum Hall liquids has been a long-standing open question. Here, we investigate this question for zero-field, electron and hole Wigner solids in cadmium arsenide quantum wells. In the low temperature limit, our results are consistent with a recent theoretical model [A. P. Reddy and L. Fu, Phys. Rev. B 113, L161403 (2026)] that proposes that the quantum Hall liquid can become energetically favored over the solid at low integer filling factors. Going beyond the low-temperature limit, we observe a re-entrant solid that emerges from the quantum Hall liquid. We explain this observation by considering the role of spin entropy, in close analogy with the zero-field Pomeranchuk effect, but appearing here at finite fields. The competition between quantum Hall liquids and Wigner solids is thus governed by both energy and entropy terms, giving rise to rich phase stability diagrams that result from the interplay between topology and correlations.
item.dc:creator: Boliang Liu, Simon Munyan, Sina Ahadi, Erez Berg, Susanne Stemmer

item.title: Axis-selective AC magnetic-field imaging in the tens-of-megahertz regime using RF-dressed continuous-wave scanning NV magnetometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.17366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatially resolved magnetic-field imaging reveals material properties and local currents in microelectronic devices. Conventional pulsed scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) magnetometry (SNVM) faces increasingly stringent microwave (MW) pulse-control requirements for detecting radio-frequency (RF) magnetic fields at frequencies ranging from tens to hundreds of megahertz. To address this challenge, we implement an RF-dressed continuous-wave (CW) sensing scheme for SNVM and demonstrate AC magnetic-field imaging at 33.5 MHz. The method exploits electron-spin double resonance in the NV spin-1 three-level system: the target RF magnetic field coherently couples two spin eigenstates, forming RF-dressed states whose splittings are detected in continuous-wave electron-spin double resonance (CW-ESDR) spectra under continuous laser, MW, and RF excitation. This approach avoids short, high-power MW pulses and synchronization between the RF field and a pulsed sensing sequence. Using an NV-ensemble diamond probe integrated with an atomic force microscope (AFM), we image the Oersted field of an RF-driven L-shaped microcircuit. Successively selecting three crystallographic NV axes by static bias-field control yields maps of RF magnetic-field projection magnitudes, with distinct distributions qualitatively reproduced by Biot-Savart calculations. Transverse bias-field control also tunes the RF-coupled spin-state transition frequency from 14.4 to 89.3 MHz, as characterized by spectroscopy and Hamiltonian analysis, with RF-dressed resonances directly observed in CW-ESDR spectra at 89.3 MHz. Together with previous RF magnetic-field detection up to 632 MHz using the same RF-dressed CW sensing principle in a confocal NV setup, these results support extending AC magnetic-field imaging with SNVM toward the hundreds-of-megahertz regime and, with additional phase information, vector magnetic-field reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Shuntaro Komuro, Ryusei Okaniwa, Kazuma Okura, Kunitaka Hayashi, Toshu An, Junko Ishi-Hayase

item.title: Narrow-Band Magnetism Allowed by Quantum Geometry: Altermagnetism and Beyond
item.description: arXiv:2611.17414v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum geometry plays a central role in shaping correlated phases in narrow bands, yet its influence on the competition between distinct magnetic orders, especially the emergence of altermagnetism, remains largely unexplored. To address this question, we study the quadrupole insulator model with strictly onsite generalized Hubbard-Kanamori interactions, in which both N\'eel antiferromagnetism and altermagnetism are symmetry-permitted. Depending on the parameters, the isolated narrow lowest band of the model can either be obstructed atomic with strong quantum geometry or trivial atomic with weak quantum geometry, while the dispersion is identical in the two cases. By partially filling the lowest band, our Hartree-Fock calculations show only conventional ferromagnetic phases for the weak quantum geometric case, while we find two collinear altermagnetic phases, as well as nematic phases, for the strong quantum geometric case. Such a dramatic difference can be understood by the distinct characters of the projected interaction: the projected interactions acquire sizable longer-range channels only for the strong quantum geometric case, while they are dominated by the on-site Hubbard channel in the weak quantum geometric case. These results establish the essential role of quantum geometry for altermagnetism to emerge from interacting narrow bands where crystalline symmetries cannot sufficiently constrain the magnetic order.
item.dc:creator: Minxuan Wang, Pei-Han Lin, Yang Ge, Jiabin Yu

item.title: Probing Spatiotemporal Quantum Correlations with Two-Qubit Relaxometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.17509v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum impurities and spin qubits are powerful local probes of magnetic fluctuations, but conventional relaxometry reduces their information to a local relaxation rate at a single frequency. Building on advances in two-qubit sensing of spatial correlations, we show how two complementary protocols probe finite-time correlations in interacting quantum matter. Phase-cycled Bell-state relaxometry isolates the signed contribution of correlated relaxation to the joint ground-state population. To second order in the probe-environment coupling, the resulting population contrast measures a finite-time integral of the energy-ordered cross-correlator. In the longitudinal regime, XY8 covariance probes the complementary symmetrized cross-correlator within a tunable frequency window. For a gapless quantum spin chain, the signals reveal interaction-dependent algebraic scaling and ballistic propagation. Luttinger-liquid theory links sign changes as the qubit frequency is swept to the propagation time between the probes. It also predicts distinct spatial power laws for the Bell signal before the correlation front and at late times, when the sensing window resolves the qubit frequency. Matrix-product-state calculations for the spin chain test the pre-front scaling at zero and finite magnetization and extract the propagation velocity from Bell oscillations at zero magnetization. The probe coupling geometry determines which spin and momentum sectors contribute to the measured signals.
item.dc:creator: Christina Psaroudaki

item.title: Equilibrium Elongation of Charged Nanoclusters
item.description: arXiv:2611.17513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When internal electrostatic stresses from electron repulsions overcome surface tension, charged nanoclusters elongate. However, the exact shape they reach at equilibrium has been unknown. We present an analytical model for the equilibrium structure of charged ellipsoidal nanoclusters via a free energy analysis. Energy maps are constructed that determine the equilibrium states as a function of cluster size, net charge, surface tension, and local curvature. The model is compared with molecular dynamics simulations of ice nanoclusters having solvated electrons. Despite the discreteness of the simulated atoms and electrons, both the predictions of the continuum analytical model for elongation and the equilibrium elongated shape show good agreement. The model could therefore predict nanocluster shape evolution in astrophysical and laboratory complex plasmas and atmospheric aerosols.
item.dc:creator: Efstratios M. Kritikos, William A. Goddard III, Paul M. Bellan

item.title: Deformation Kinetics of Charged Nanoclusters via Surface Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2611.17514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Low-temperature charged nanoclusters deform, primarily via surface diffusion, when surface electrostatic stresses and surface tension stresses are not balanced. We derive an analytical model for the kinetics of this process, based on the cluster size, net charge, surface tension, local curvature, temperature, and diffusivity. The model predicts the deformation time when either surface tension or electrostatic stress dominates, leading respectively to the collapse or elongation of the cluster. Comparison with molecular dynamics simulations of ice nanoclusters with solvated electrons shows quantitative agreement with a single fitted parameter. The model can predict the deformation kinetics of charged nanoclusters in atmospheric aerosols and complex plasmas.
item.dc:creator: Efstratios M. Kritikos, William A. Goddard III, Paul M. Bellan

item.title: Quantum Fluctuations drive Emerging Bosonic Quantum Phases in a Moir\'e Flatband Superconductor
item.description: arXiv:2611.17882v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum fluctuations play a central role in superconductors by mediating the interactions that promote electron pairing and controlling the phase coherence required for macroscopic condensation. Thus far, understanding the interplay between quantum fluctuations and superconductivity remains challenging in unconventional superconductors. Here, we establish quantum phase fluctuations as the organizing principle linking superconductivity and Bose-insulating quantum criticality in a moir\'e flatband superconductor of alternating twisted trilayer graphene (ATTG). Superconductivity is optimal near half-filling of the moir\'e flatband and gives way to a density-wave-like resistance peak at high temperatures, in which we observe distinct temperature scales for the pairing (~6 K) and the condensation (~1 K). We observe compelling evidence of a bosonic superconducting quantum phase transition, driven by both out-of-plane and in-plane magnetic fields, with a universal critical resistivity of $R_c =~0.62R_Q$ and finite-temperature scaling of $z{\nu}_B = 2.3$, where $R_Q = h/4e^2$ is the quantum resistance for bosons. Strikingly, the observed bosonic insulator shows a nearly quantized resistivity of $R_Q$ that saturates at low temperatures and high magnetic fields, together with a zero-bias peak, a nearly zero Hall resistance, and a logarithmic dependence at higher temperatures. Both the superconductor and the bosonic insulator could be driven into the same critical quantum fluctuation regime dynamically under a large bias. Our results establish moir\'e flatband as a clean platform for studying unconventional superconductivity and bosonic quantum criticality governed by quantum fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Yu Hong, Haiming Sun, Qixing Zhang, Le Liu, Zitian Pan, Jundong Zhu, Jingwei Dong, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Luojun Du, Dongxia Shi, Adrian Bachtold, Haiwen Liu, Guangyu Zhang, Wei Yang

item.title: Influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and periodicity on giant chiral asymmetry of domain wall mobility in epitaxial Cu/Pd/Co/Pd(111) films
item.description: arXiv:2611.17932v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity on the chirality-dependent mobility of domain walls (DWs) in epitaxial Si(111)/Cu(2-7 nm)/Pd(3 nm)/Co(0.7 nm)/Pd(3 nm) heterostructures. By varying the Cu buffer layer thickness, we systematically modify the morphology of the magnetic interfaces while maintaining a constant composition and thickness of the Pd/Co/Pd trilayer. Scanning tunneling microscopy reveals that increasing the Cu thickness leads to the development of a hierarchical interfacial morphology characterized by increasing roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity. We observe a dramatic enhancement of the asymmetry between the velocities of DWs with opposite chirality in the creep regime, reaching a velocity ratio of approximately 50000 in the sample with a 7-nm-thick Cu buffer layer. This value exceeds by more than an order of magnitude the effective saturated asymmetry previously observed in Pd/Co/Pd structures with roughness controlled by the bottom Pd layer thickness. Despite comparable root-mean-square interface roughness in both series, the Cu-buffer-induced morphology exhibits a substantially larger characteristic lateral periodicity. We propose that the enhanced asymmetry originates from the different spatial organization of interfacial disorder, which modifies the pinning energy landscape and amplifies chirality-dependent thermally activated DW propagation. Our results suggest that engineering not only the amplitude but also the lateral spatial correlations of interfacial roughness provides an effective approach for controlling chiral DW dynamics in magnetic heterostructures.
item.dc:creator: N. N. Chernousov, A. S. Pashenko, A. G. Kozlov, A. A. Turpak, A. S. Samardak, A. V. Davydenko

item.title: Tunable coupling between valley and magnetic excitons in WS2/CrSBr heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2611.18187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interfacial coupling in van der Waals two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offers an effective route to tailor the electronic, optical, and magnetic properties of materials. Versatile control and precise engineering of such interlayer interactions can be further achieved through external parameters, like electric field, magnetic field, optical excitation, as well as layer stacking geometries. Here, we examined the magneto-optical properties of 2D semiconductor heterostructures made of antiferromagnetic CrSBr and a monolayer WS2, both of which host intriguing excitonic properties. We identified a type-II band alignment between these two layers and the magnetic proximity effects from CrSBr, manifested by an enhanced Zeeman valley splitting in the WS2 layer. The interlayer charge transfer shows strong spin selectivity and is governed by the relative alignment between the valley-spin polarization of photoexcited carriers in WS2 and the magnetization in CrSBr, giving rise to spin-sensitive circularly polarized photoluminescence (PL) from WS2. Furthermore, the highly anisotropic electronic dispersion in CrSBr enables stacking-dependent control of interlayer interactions, as inferred from a twist-angle dependence of PL quenching. Our work establishes a highly tunable 2D system that integrates valleytronics and magnetic excitons through multiple coupling channels, opening up new opportunities in all-optical manipulation of spin and magnon states and for the development of flexible spin-optoelectronic devices.
item.dc:creator: Jianchen Dang, Liza Godziashvili, Kaichen Xie, Arun Ramanathan, Vadym Kulichenko, Alejandro Busto, Jia-Yi Ji, Robert Boyd, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Sina Najmaei, Daniel Rhodes, Luis Balicas, Xavier Roy, Ting Cao, Xiao-Xiao Zhang

item.title: Bond Anharmonicity in a Caged Molecule Probed by Vibronic Core Spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2611.18331v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: X-ray absorption spectroscopy and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering at the nitrogen K-edge show that the N$\equiv$N bond in N$_2$@C$_{60}$ is substantially more anharmonic than in free N$_2$, with the ground-state ($X^1\Sigma_g^+$) anharmonic constant $\hbar\omega_e x_e$ a factor of two larger ($3.8\pm0.3$~meV versus $\sim 1.8$~meV) despite an essentially unchanged harmonic frequency. The same enhancement is found across all three vibronic potentials accessible to the experiment---the electronic ground state, the core-excited intermediate state, and the spectator-decay final state---pointing to a common origin rather than an effect specific to one electronic configuration. High-level coupled-cluster calculations of the N$_2$@C$_{60}$ potential energy surface, however, find no significant change in anharmonicity upon encapsulation, ruling out a simple static distortion of the N$\equiv$N bonding potential by the fullerene cage. We propose instead that the dramatic increase in $\hbar\omega_e x_e$ above the gas-phase value -- which, taken literally, would imply an unphysical halving of the N$_2$ dissociation energy - reflects the breakdown of the single-molecule Morse description, as previously invoked to explain anomalous anharmonicities in N$_2$ clusters, and supported by the observation of shifts in the fullerene host's Raman modes.
item.dc:creator: Connor J. B. item.title: Edge spin generalization for quantum Hall Laughlin droplets with elliptic shapes
item.description: arXiv:2611.18377v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is known that quasiparticles in the bulk of quantum Hall systems possess an emergent spin, which satisfies a spin-statistics relation. Recent results show that this spin can fractionalize: a quasiparticle spin in the bulk induces an opposite edge spin on the boundary. So far, the edge spin has only been studied in the simplest possible geometries, where the boundary is either circular or straight, without considering that a generic confining potential could give the droplet a non-symmetric shape. Yet, the value of the edge spin is not dictated by symmetry, but by topology: it is expected that the specific shape of the edge should not matter. In this work, we therefore generalize the edge spin to elliptically shaped droplets. We consider two different generalizations of the edge spin and test them on a family of elliptic Laughlin states introduced in the present work. The first, most straightforward, generalization is based on the properties of the single-particle orbitals for the elliptic confining potential. We show that this proposal applies to non-interacting states. The second proposal is based on the emergent properties of the quantum fluid. We show that this proposal also applies to interacting states, making it the suitable definition of the edge spin in the elliptic case. Our work demonstrates that it is possible to define an edge spin for Laughlin fluids with a non-trivial shape.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Fagerlund, Alberto Nardin, Leonardo Mazza, Eddy Ardonne

item.title: Uniaxial strain induces $d$-wave phonon chirality in ferroelectric BaTiO$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.18402v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Circularly dichroic resonant inelastic x-ray scattering has revealed electrically switchable $g$-wave phonon chirality in freestanding BaTiO$_3$ membranes. Here, we show from first principles that uniaxial strain changes the angular class of this texture. Lowering $C_{4v}$ to $C_{2v}$ adds a $d$-wave helicity that is bilinear in the orthorhombic strain $\eta$ and the polarization, with nodal lines along the stress axis. For the 38~meV branches at $\eta=1\%$, we find that (i) along the diagonal, where the helicity vanishes by symmetry without strain, it reaches about 60\% of the unstrained maximum, and (ii) at the measured wave vectors off the mirror it is reduced by more than half. With PBEsol and PBE+D3 force constants, the $d$-wave component grows linearly in $\eta$ and equals the $g$-wave one at $\eta^*\approx1.3\text{--}1.4\%$. Resolved by branch, the response of strain-split $E$ doublets is non-analytic in $\eta$, as captured by a two-band model. Strain therefore provides a second knob, besides the electric field, that controls the symmetry and the sign of phonon chirality in ferroelectric membranes.
item.dc:creator: Juan M. Florez, Eric Su\'arez Morell

item.title: Graph diffusion transformer for interpretable generation and inverse design of disordered atomic structures
item.description: arXiv:2611.18420v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Atomic disorder offers a potent degree of freedom to tailor material properties, yet the resulting vast configuration space obscures structure-property relations and hinders rational inverse design. Here we introduce Graph Amorphous Diffusion Transformer (GaDiT), a generative model that combines dynamic periodic graphs, masked conditioning and an interval-weighted training-noise distribution. GaDiT generates high-quality disordered structures while accelerating sampling by two orders of magnitude compared with existing corrector-based approaches, as demonstrated across two-dimensional amorphous carbon and three-dimensional amorphous silicon and silica. Moreover, GaDiT supports conditional generation under single or combined structural features, physical properties and preparation conditions in a unified model, and enables inverse design that expands accessible structure-property ranges beyond the training distribution. To interpret these structures and the trained network, we propose a conditioned atomic response mapping analysis, revealing both the global structural descriptors and the local atomic environments that govern target properties. Overall, GaDiT establishes a general framework for interpretable generation, inverse design and structure-property discovery for disordered atomic structures.
item.dc:creator: Jiani Hu, Chenyan Wang, Yongkun Yang, Guanyu Hou, Jihaochen Zhang, Lei Liu, Ji Chen

item.title: Dissipation as a Resource for Entanglement via High-Spin Mediator Purification
item.description: arXiv:2611.18489v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study entanglement generation between two spin qubits mediated by a single, thermally mixed, high-spin ($S=5/2$) magnetic impurity, using the Lindblad master equation to compare coherent and dissipative control of the mediator. We show that no coherent drive, however strong or resonant, can purify the mediator beyond its thermal value --- a direct consequence of unitary evolution exactly preserving state purity --- while a dissipative channel purifies it up to the limit set by the optical pumping cycle itself, $\mathrm{Tr}[\rho_M^2]\approx0.8$. Modeling this channel with rates fixed by the measured optical pumping of a single Mn spin, we find that the entanglement it enables is not monotonic in the pump strength: it peaks at a finite rate and then decreases, since the same channel leaks decoherence to the qubits through the coupling that mediates their entanglement. At the experimental pumping rate, a single $80$ns pulse purifies the mediator, the resulting polarization persists for a timescale three orders of magnitude longer than the entangling dynamics, and the first-recurrence negativity rises from $0.18$ to $0.64$ at $12$K, remaining above $0.6$ up to $30$K. These results establish dissipation, not as noise to be suppressed, but as the very resource that makes robust entanglement generation possible.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Martins Fernandes, Fabricio Macedo de Souza

item.title: Hall resistance under a non-Hermitian linear potential
item.description: arXiv:2502.14579v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate how a non-Hermitian linear perturbation modifies Landau states and Hall transport, combining an exact continuum solution with numerical tight-binding calculations on a finite square lattice. The analytical solution yields energy branches with a complex linear Stark shift. A conserved non-Hermitian guiding-center operator identifies coherent states and determines the orbit center through its eigenvalue. The continuum model admits states with balanced gain and loss whose energies remain real at any perturbation strength. Finite-lattice calculations support the Landau-level structure and exhibit eigenvalue coalescences followed by the emergence of imaginary parts, consistent with exceptional points. Finally, transport calculations at a fixed injection energy show a shift of the Hall resistance plateaus moving them linearly from the von Klitzing constant.
item.dc:creator: Kenan Uriostegui, Santiago Galv\'an-y-Garc\'ia, Thomas Stegmann, Jorge Lizarraga

item.title: Topological phase transitions between bosonic and fermionic quantum Hall states near even-denominator filling factors
item.description: arXiv:2508.17457v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the quantum critical point between the fermionic $\nu=8$ quantum Hall state and the bosonic $\nu=2$ quantum Hall state of Cooper pairs. Our study is motivated by the composite fermion construction for the daughter states of even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states and the experimentally observed transition between the daughter and the Jain states at the same filling. We show that this transition is equivalent to the transition between a neutral invertible $E_8$ state and a topologically trivial state. These transitions can be described in a partonic framework as a cascade of mass changes of four neutral Dirac fermions coupled to multiple Abelian Chern--Simons $U(1)$ gauge fields. In the absence of fine-tuning, the transition is split into a series of at least eight distinct transitions, with at least seven distinct intermediate topologically ordered phases that host neutral anyons.
item.dc:creator: Evgenii Zheltonozhskii, Ady Stern, Netanel H. Lindner

item.title: Puiseux series about exceptional singularities dictated by symmetry-allowed Hessenberg forms of perturbation matrices
item.description: arXiv:2603.25603v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a systematic framework for determining the nature of exceptional points of $n^{\rm th}$ order (EP$_n$s) in non-Hermitian (NH) systems, represented by complex square matrices. By expressing symmetry-preserving perturbations ($\propto \epsilon$) in the Jordan-normal basis of the defective matrix at an EP$_n$, we show that the upper-$\ell$ Hessenberg structure of the perturbation matrix directly dictates the leading-order eigenvalue- and eigenvector-splitting to be $\propto \epsilon^{1/\ell}$, when expanded in a Puiseux series. Applying this to three-band NH models invariant under parity (P), charge-conjugation (C), or parity-time-reversal (PT), we find that EP$_3$s in P- and C-symmetric systems are restricted to at most $\sim \epsilon^{1/2}$ branch points, while PT-symmetric systems generically support EP$_3$s with the strongest possible singularities (viz. $\sim \epsilon^{1/3}$). We illustrate these results with concrete three-dimensional models in which exceptional curves and surfaces emerge. We further show that fine-tuned perturbations can suppress the leading-order branch point to a less-singular splitting, which have implications for designing direction-dependent EP-based sensors. The appendix extends the analysis to four-band P- and C-symmetric models, establishing the existence of EP$_4$s with $\sim \epsilon^{1/4}$ and $\sim \epsilon^{1/2}$ singularities, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Ipsita Mandal

item.title: How Superradiance Survives Molecular Noise inside Virus Capsids
item.description: arXiv:2610.00739v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Excited organic dyes chemically bound to an icosahedral virus shell can spontaneously synchronize and emit a superradiant burst of light. The mechanism that allows it to occur at room temperature, despite collisional dephasing and inhomogeneous broadening, is not understood. Few other known low-dimensional condensed matter systems exhibit room-temperature superradiance (SR). In the fluctuation-prone environment of molecular-based systems, electron--vibrational coupling has been proposed to play a central role. Here, we addressed experimentally the existence of underdamped virus capsid phonon-like modes and theoretically their involvement in the transition from uncorrelated to cooperative emission. We find that SR-active dye-labeled capsids exhibit underdamped low-frequency oscillations that modulate the dye excited-state response, and modeling shows how such capsid motion can promote the collective polarization required for superradiant emission.
item.dc:creator: Tianran Li, Irina Tsvetkova, Matthew Brauser, Amala Raj, Grace L. Clemmer, Philip Shushkov, Bogdan Dragnea

item.title: Adjoint-State Identifiability of Piezo-Tunable Valley Splitting in 2D Magnetic Heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2610.07179v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mechanical strain has been proposed to dynamically tune proximity-induced valley splitting in 2D magnetic heterostructures for solid-state information processing. While first-principles studies routinely predict strain-modulated valley splittings at the atomic scale, they rarely address whether the coupling parameter can be extracted from a macroscopic transport measurement against realistic device noise. This paper develops a classical, partial differential equation-constrained multiscale inverse framework to quantify the device-level identifiability of the exchange-strain coupling from a transverse Hall voltage in a molybdenum disulfide and chromium tribromide heterostructure. Structural relaxation confirms a chiral $C_3$ point-group symmetry of the Hollow-stacked structure, and Neumann's principle reduces the coupling tensor to a single scalar $\eta$. Dispersion-corrected density functional theory gives a zero-strain splitting of -0.45 meV and bounds the coupling to $|\eta| \lesssim 2$ meV at small tensile strain while leaving its sign open, motivating the transport analysis. For an example coupling of $|\eta| = 0.56$ meV, where an actuator strain trace of $3.5 \times 10^{-4}$ shifts the valley splitting by only 0.2 $\mu$eV, operation at 10 K below the Curie temperature of CrBr$_3$ makes the coupling statistically resolvable from 5.6 to 3,704 V/cm. Even in a demanding stress test recovering $\eta$ jointly with the zero-strain splitting, an uncalibrated Hall gain, and an unknown intervalley scattering time, the window spans 25 to 3,704 V/cm and the Cram\'er-Rao bound at the 10% velocity-saturation limit reaches 13.6 $\mu$eV, 21 times below the resolution criterion. Since this window covers the full operational bias range of 2D field-effect transistors, from low-power linear readout to high-field drive, this framework serves as a pre-fabrication diagnostic for valleytronic devices.
item.dc:creator: Suhas Suresh Bharadwaj

item.title: Imaging spin entanglement with a scanning tunneling microscope
item.description: arXiv:2611.10946v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Artificial spin arrays assembled on surfaces enable atomic-scale studies of quantum correlations. Here we establish a hierarchy of connections between spin inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy (IETS) and entanglement in spin-$1/2$ systems. We first show that the number of spectroscopically active transitions in a spin-$1/2$ dimer serves as an entanglement witness. Using the leading-order tunneling conductance for the tip placed on spin $i$, $dI(i)/dV$, we then relate spectral moments $\mathcal{M}^{(n)}(i)=\int V^n(d^2I(i)/dV^2)\,dV$ to quantum correlations. The zeroth moment probes the one-tangle in systems with a gapped, nondegenerate ground state. For rotationally invariant Heisenberg systems, the first moment yields thermal spin correlators $\langle\boldsymbol S(i)\cdot\boldsymbol S(j)\rangle$, enabling reconstruction of nearest-neighbor concurrence and spatial imaging of entanglement in spin chains. It also provides access to the internal energy and magnetic specific heat, both usable as entanglement witnesses. Applying this approach to experimental IETS data from nanographene spin chains, we find good agreement with theory. We further discuss how the second moment probes longer-range correlations and the inverse moment relates to local spin susceptibility. For spin-$1/2$ trimers, we connect inter-multiplet inelastic spectral weight to genuine tripartite entanglement quantified by the concurrence fill. Finally, we reconcile the local character of IETS with its sensitivity to nonlocal entanglement through an analogy with digital quantum circuits, where Hamiltonian evolution implements multiqubit operations. These results establish IETS as a tool for quantifying and imaging entanglement in engineered on-surface spin systems.
item.dc:creator: J. C. G. Henriques, B. Vi\~na-Baus\'a, I. Brihuega, J. Fern\'andez-Rossier

item.title: Exotic superconducting states in altermagnets
item.description: arXiv:2507.10700v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The interplay between magnetism and superconductivity is one of the central topics of condensed matter physics, which has recently been put into new light by the discovery of altermagnets. Here, we study this interplay from a fundamental symmetry perspective using irreducible co-representations of the altermagnetic spin-point groups. We construct and tabulate all symmetry-allowed pairing functions for altermagnets, which uncovers numerous exotic pairing states. We focus on three of them, namely: (i) a non-unitary ``altermagnetic superconductor'' with different spatial anisotropies for the spin-up and spin-down condensates, (ii) a ``half-and-half metal-superconductor" where only electrons with one of the two spin components form Cooper pairs, and (iii) a ``spin chiral superconductor'' with spin-polarized chiral edge states. Interestingly, the first of these three superconductors exhibits an unusual fractional ac Josephson current for only one of the two spin polarizations, even though the two condensates are symmetry related. We present phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau theories for these unconventional superconductors and show that they correspond to stable minima of the free energies. We examine their topological properties, study the effects of small spin-orbit coupling, consider possible material examples, and investigate their topological responses.
item.dc:creator: Kirill Parshukov, Andreas P. Schnyder

item.title: Scalable topological quantum computing based on Sine-Cosine chain models
item.description: arXiv:2603.25952v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a scalable framework for quantum information processing based on Matryoshka-type sine-cosine chains, a hierarchy of one-dimensional chiral-symmetric lattices obtained by repeated ($P$ times) square-root construction starting from the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain. A chain of order $P$ can host $2^{P+2}-2$ protected edge states, so a single physical device can encode a qudit of equivalent dimension (or, equivalently, several independent qubits) instead of one qubit per device. We show that (i) the adiabatic defect-transfer step underlying SSH-based topological gates carries over unchanged to the Matryoshka chain, transferring the full set of defect states simultaneously; (ii) a Y-junction braiding protocol then composes single-qudit gate operations in all energy sectors at once, increasing the operation density per physical device; and (iii) the same edge states provide a quantum memory whose capacity scales exponentially with the chain order at fixed physical length. Numerical fidelity analysis under on-site, hopping, and correlated angle disorder shows partial, chiral-symmetry-protected robustness.
item.dc:creator: A. Lykholat, G. F. Moreira, I. R. Martins, D. Sousa, A. M. Marques, R. G. Dias

item.title: Quantum limits on squeezing
item.description: arXiv:2604.22500v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In our work, we show how, for a network of bosonic modes, canonical commutation relations constrain the coefficients relating input and internal modes. Based on these constraints, we derive a lower bound on the total steady-state squeezing achievable in reservoir-engineered (dissipative) squeezing schemes, quantified by the sum of mode-optimal quadrature variances each normalized to its corresponding input variance. The bound on this normalized sum follows solely from canonical commutation relations and stability, and is saturated in the strong-coupling limit at unity. Furthermore, we show that adding independent parametric driving terms for each mode changes the quantum noise--gain balance and yields, for the same normalized mode-optimal sum, a distinct optimum bound, approaching 1/2. In addition, we show how these constraints allow us to reformulate the Duan inseparability criterion for a three-mode bosonic system in terms of a single parameter-dependent figure of merit. Our results apply directly to current electromechanical and nanomechanical experiments and indicate that the two-mode bounds can be experimentally approached even at room temperature.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Massel

item.title: Susceptibility-kinetic uncertainty relations for quantum systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.01035v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Kinetic uncertainty relations bound current precision of stochastic processes by dynamical activity. The extension of these bounds to quantum systems has been impeded by coherence, strong system-reservoir coupling, and the subtlety of defining dynamical activity in the quantum regime. Here, we introduce a partial dynamical activity through the quantum Fisher information associated with the rescaling of the system-reservoir coupling and show that it bounds current precision via a universal susceptibility-kinetic uncertainty relation. The general validity of this relation is guaranteed by the natural contribution of a susceptibility term, which is experimentally accessible by tuning the system-reservoir coupling strength. We show how the partial dynamical activity encompasses previous definitions of activity in the weak-coupling Markovian limit and that it provides an information-geometric interpretation of correlator-based activities. We illustrate the tight constraint on precision that our bound provides with the example of the dynamics of a strongly interacting finite-size system and of steady-state coherent transport through a double quantum dot, where quantum effects invalidate previously developed kinetic uncertainty relations. We expect our bound to provide a powerful tool for optimizing precision in arbitrary quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Didrik Palmqvist, Janine Splettstoesser, Ludovico Tesser

item.title: Altermagnetism across the BCS-BEC crossover
item.description: arXiv:2609.14613v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a two-dimensional paired Fermi system in which altermagnetism produces a spin splitting that depends on momentum. The interaction strength is described through the two-body binding energy, so that the chemical potential and pairing gap evolve self-consistently from the weak-coupling Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) regime to the strong-coupling Bose-Einstein-condensate (BEC) regime at fixed density. The stability of the uniform paired state is examined by giving the pairs a small center-of-mass momentum and following the resulting change in free energy. We show that at zero temperature, the phase stiffness follows a universal quadratic suppression, $J/J_0 = 1 - (\alpha/\alpha_0)^2$, across the entire fully gapped crossover regime. Deviations from this relation emerge only on the BCS side upon the opening of gapless Bogoliubov pockets, which rapidly reduce the stiffness and can trigger an instability toward finite-momentum pairing. In the BEC regime, this universal quadratic correction corresponds to the altered effective mass of the tightly bound composite bosons. The model therefore provides a simple setting in which to compare altermagnetic pair breaking on the BCS and BEC sides of the crossover.
item.dc:creator: Iogann Tolbatov, Luca Salasnich

item.title: Macroscopic Nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer Mediated by Coherent Magnons
item.description: arXiv:2610.31507v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Phonon-mediated nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer (RET) in metal deuterides is severely constrained by inertial rest-mass dilution, lattice fracture limits, and thermal nuclear spin cancellation. Extending the generalized nuclear Dicke model to Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) magnons eliminates mass dilution via hyperfine-amplified M1 coupling while unlocking relativistic Dirac M2 coupling via Overhauser spin polarization. We derive a Suhl-clamped FMR scaling law predicting 14.2 MeV (Pd-106) and 11.4 MeV (Ni-58) breakup neutrons, 19.9 MeV alpha particles, and reconciled sub-keV fusion anomalies.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Weed
